newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine blue chips retreat to finish flat.
newsitem.headline: Argentine blue chips retreat to finish flat.

text.p: Argentine leading stocks surrendered slim early gains to close flat Friday, but forecasts were fairly optimistic.

"This week we had options expirations, and there was normal tension in the markets," said Rafael Aldazabal of traders Aldazabal. "But stocks ended on a firm note because they were able to digest the week's political events."
He blamed the pullback late in the session on what he called the "Friday syndrome" of low liquidity on Wall Street.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV closed flat at 569.65, after hitting 573.4, showing a 2.5 percent loss for the week.
The index had closed higher in the previous seven consecutive weeks, amassing gains of nearly 15 percent since late August.

Traders said a political scandal unleashed Tuesday by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, who blamed two government ministers of covering up corruption cases and hand-picking judges, had triggered a stronger-than-expected downwards correction on the market.
"The political row caused profit-taking to pick up speed," said Aldazabal. "But stocks recovered some of the lost ground (Thursday) and fell back in line with Latin American markets."
Traders said investors remained wary of new recent international market-moving factors such as financial jitters in Mexico and political uncertainty in Russia.
"The focus of some of the big market players is shifting more to foreign factors, so they remain cautious," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
Floor volume rose to 17.5 million pesos in the session from 16.2 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 124.5 million pesos against 144.7 million Thursday.
The bolsa's broad market dipped 0.1 percent, although winners edged out losers 20 to 25 and 26 stocks closed flat.

The day's best main-tier performers were construction stock Juan Minetti, which jumped 2.7 percent, steelmaker Acindar, which climbed 2.1 percent, and oil company Astra, sugar refiner Ledesma and Banco Frances, all up 1.7 percent.
Losers were led by oil company Sol Petroleo, power utility Central Puerto and carmaker Sevel, which fell 5.2 percent, 3.2 percent and 2.0 percent, respectively.
